Exact_Sentence: Introduction
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Tactical occupations combine routine occupational exposures with periods of abrupt, mission-critical demand.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Law-enforcement officers, firefighters, military personnel, and other tactical professionals may be required to transition from prolonged vigilance or administrative activity to high-intensity exertion, threat processing, casualty care, armed decision-making, or team-based action with little warning.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This combination means that readiness cannot be reduced to aerobic capacity, strength, absence of disease, or technical proficiency in isolation.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Total Force Fitness already conceptualized readiness at the unit level as an interaction among demands, resources, and outcomes, while the 2026 ACC/AHA scientific statement on tactical athletes emphasized task-specific cardiovascular demands, environmental and situational strain amplifiers, and the operational consequences of incapacitation.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: These precedents support a multidimensional view, but they do not resolve how heterogeneous evidence from public-safety systems should be integrated without overstating causality, transferability, or measurement validity.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Brazil provides a useful adaptation case because public safety is decentralized across state institutions, missions differ between police and fire services, training systems are heterogeneous, and available research spans nutrition, shooting, academy fitness, tactical medicine, occupational health, and policy evaluation.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The same heterogeneity that makes the evidence informative also creates a high risk of overgeneralization: a small police sample from one state cannot define a national nutrition norm; cadet shooting data cannot be treated as field performance; a state medical cohort cannot estimate national prevalence; and documentation of tourniquet use cannot establish survival benefit.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The methodological problem is therefore not simply to summarize studies, but to preserve the inferential boundary of each study while building a coherent operational picture.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The objective of this work was to develop a claim-locked narrative evidence synthesis of operational readiness in tactical populations, using Brazilian public-safety evidence as a bounded adaptation layer.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The synthesis was designed to keep null findings visible, prevent double counting of overlapping cohorts, separate central from contextual evidence, and fail closed when integrity was unresolved.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Its output is a proposed synthesis framework intended for evidence organization and research planning.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: It is explicitly not a validated readiness score, diagnostic instrument, fitness-for-duty algorithm, or predictive model.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Conceptual Background
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: For this synthesis, operational readiness is defined as the state in which an individual and the surrounding organization retain sufficient health, physical capacity, cognitive and technical performance, medical capability, and organizational support to meet mission demands within an acceptable risk envelope.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This is a project-level integrative definition, not a replacement for Total Force Fitness or tactical clinical management.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The demand-resource logic of Total Force Fitness is relevant because occupational outcomes emerge from interactions between mission demands and available personal or organizational resources.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The ACC/AHA tactical-athlete statement adds a complementary clinical perspective by emphasizing that the same task can impose different cardiovascular loads depending on heat, dehydration, chronic alertness, equipment, recovery, and other strain amplifiers.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: These external frameworks establish two important constraints on the present model.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: First, multidomain readiness is not a novel concept.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Second, readiness must remain linked to task context rather than being treated as a single latent trait that can be measured by one score without validation.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Accordingly, the synthesis separates eight analytic components: nutrition and schedule load; cognition and firearm-task performance; tactical-medicine practice readiness; organizational and policy readiness; physical and academy readiness; medical readiness; contextual physiological mechanisms; and evidence governance/change control.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The first six organize direct or near-direct public-safety evidence, the seventh contains mechanistic or indirectly transferable evidence, and the eighth exists to prevent evidence-role drift.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The framework is therefore deliberately asymmetric.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Some domains contain direct Brazilian police data but weak causal designs; others contain stronger quasi-experimental policy designs but outcomes that are organizational rather than physiological; tactical medicine has operational-use documentation but lacks verified comparative patient-outcome evidence; and implementation science remains structurally underdeveloped in the mapped Brazilian literature.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This unevenness is not treated as a defect to be hidden.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: It is treated as information about where the evidence base is mature, where it is only descriptive, and where future validation work is required.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Evidence Architecture
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The frozen architecture is intentionally heterogeneous.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The nine Core records span seven substantive domains: two nutrition/shift-work studies; two firearm-performance publications from a partially overlapping cadet family; one operational tourniquet-use study; two policy/program evaluations; one academy-fitness study; and one medical-readiness cohort.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The Supporting record concerns supplemental martial-arts experience and simulated use-of-force performance.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Contextual records include Brazilian APH-Tático material, the national institutional APH-Tático framework, military patrol physiology, and police mental-health promotion.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This architecture matters because conventional narrative synthesis can inadvertently flatten study design.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Here, a cross-sectional association, an uncontrolled longitudinal change, a difference-in-differences policy estimate, a qualitative institutional analysis, and a simulated performance comparison are not treated as equivalent.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Instead, the synthesis asks what each design can legitimately contribute to readiness.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Cross-sectional work can identify associations and potential monitoring targets; uncontrolled longitudinal work can document change over time but not isolate a causal training component; quasi-experimental policy evaluation can estimate organizational outcomes under identification assumptions but cannot establish physiological readiness; and contextual material can describe institutional structures without being used as proof of effectiveness.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The result is an evidence map rather than an effect-size hierarchy.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This is appropriate for a multidomain occupational construct in which outcomes are not commensurable: reaction time, caloric intake, shooting accuracy, tourniquet use, homicide rates, physical-fitness tests, medical readiness, and simulated use-of-force scores cannot be defensibly pooled into one quantitative readiness estimate.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The evidence architecture therefore prioritizes traceability, domain-specific interpretation, and explicit non-inference.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Nutrition and Schedule Load
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The nutrition domain is anchored by two observational studies of Brazilian military police working shifts in the northern region.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Brito and colleagues studied 22 officers using 24-hour dietary recalls and the Psychomotor Vigilance Test.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: During day shifts, higher caloric intake correlated with more attention lapses (r=0.630) and slower mean reaction time (r=0.565); protein intake was also associated with lapses and reaction time at the beginning and end of the shift.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: During night shifts, psychomotor performance declined, but caloric and macronutrient intake were not significantly correlated with those performance measures.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The design is cross-sectional and the sample is small; therefore, the result supports an association between intake patterns and selected vigilance metrics under specific shift conditions, not a claim that higher caloric or protein intake causes impaired police performance.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: A second study evaluated 34 military police officers and compared dietary intake and meal timing across day shifts, night shifts, and off-duty days.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Median energy intake was higher on day-shift days than on night-shift or off-duty days (2781 versus 2350 and 2295 kcal), with corresponding differences in protein and lipid intake; the eating window also differed by work schedule.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: These findings add a chrononutritional dimension to readiness: occupational schedules are associated not only with when officers eat but also with the amount and composition of intake.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Yet the evidence does not support a national dietary prescription, nor does it demonstrate that changing meal timing improves operational outcomes.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Taken together, the two studies suggest that schedule and nutrition should be considered jointly when monitoring readiness.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The stronger inference is not that a particular macronutrient target optimizes performance, but that shift-dependent eating behavior and vigilance can vary together in operational populations.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This distinction is important for intervention design.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: A future program should prospectively measure sleep, workload, dietary timing, total intake, environmental conditions, and task performance rather than treating nutrition as an isolated exposure.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: It should also avoid assuming that patterns observed in Acre generalize to different police systems, climates, schedules, or demographic profiles.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Cognition and Firearm-Task Performance
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Firearm-task performance is represented by two publications from a partially overlapping Espírito Santo Military Police cadet cohort family.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: In the stress-symptom study, 24 third-year officer cadets were classified according to the presence of stress symptoms.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Shooting was assessed using a standardized defensive-shooting evaluation at 5 m, and handgrip strength was measured in dominant, non-dominant, and shooting positions.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Shooting time, total score, and the derived accuracy metric did not differ significantly between groups.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Handgrip strength in the shooting position was lower in cadets with stress symptoms, whereas dominant and non-dominant handgrip measures were not significantly different.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The bounded conclusion is therefore that the tested stress-symptom classification was associated with a position-specific grip-strength difference but not with a detectable decrement in the measured shooting outcomes under that protocol.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The second publication assessed 26 military police officers and examined relationships among institutional physical-fitness indicators, handgrip strength, mood state, body-mass-related variables, and firearm proficiency.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Overall physical-fitness indicators did not show a consistent global correlation with shooting proficiency; selected associations were observed for dominant handgrip strength, body-mass-related variables, and mood vigor.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This does not mean that physical fitness is irrelevant to armed policing.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The shooting task samples a narrow performance domain, and fitness may affect mobility, fatigue tolerance, casualty movement, use of force, heat strain, or the capacity to repeat high-intensity tasks without being strongly correlated with a short firearm test.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The cohort-overlap rule is methodologically important.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The two publications answer different questions, but they cannot be counted as two independent replications that a broad category such as 'fitness' does not affect shooting.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The appropriate synthesis is narrower: within the studied cadet/officer samples and protocols, gross physical-fitness measures were not consistently aligned with firearm score, while specific psychophysiological or strength variables showed selected relationships.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Operational validation would require independent cohorts, ecologically valid scenarios, repeated-measures designs, and performance outcomes that capture decision quality, accuracy, time, movement, threat discrimination, and safety under fatigue or stress.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Tactical Medicine Readiness
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The tactical-medicine domain illustrates the difference between operational documentation and clinical effectiveness.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Matos and Santos combined documentary/normative analysis with PMMG occurrence records from 2013-2017 and 2020-2024.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The study documented tourniquet use by military police in third parties, with civilian victims representing more than 90% of recorded applications, and described increased use after the institutionalization of training.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: For this synthesis, those records establish that tourniquets were operationally used and that the practice was institutionally relevant.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: They do not establish survival benefit, mortality reduction, comparative effectiveness, appropriateness in every case, or the causal effect of training.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Contextual sources reinforce that APH-Tático has an institutional and doctrinal presence in Brazilian public safety.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: A Paraná-focused qualitative review describes tactical prehospital care in special-operations settings, while the Ministry of Justice and Public Security maintains the national APH-Tático directive, minimum competencies, equipment guidance, and curriculum materials.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: These sources help define practice context and governance but were not promoted to effectiveness evidence.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Their role is particularly important because a mature readiness system requires not only individual medical skills but also equipment availability, protocols, training continuity, scene integration, data capture, and interfaces with the civilian emergency-care system.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The central limitation remains explicit: STRUCTURAL_EVIDENCE_GAP — BRAZILIAN PATIENT-OUTCOME TACTICAL MEDICINE.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The frozen evidence set contains operational-use documentation but no robust verified comparative patient-outcome study demonstrating the effect of tactical-medicine implementation on survival, hemorrhage control, disability, time to definitive care, or preventable death in Brazilian public-safety operations.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Closing this gap requires interoperable registries linking scene variables, interventions, provider role, injury characteristics, transport, hospital outcomes, and training exposure.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Until such data exist, tactical-medicine readiness should be discussed as capability and documented practice, not as proven patient-outcome effectiveness.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Organizational and Policy Readiness
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Organizational readiness is supported by policy evidence with substantially different designs.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Parfitt and colleagues evaluated results-based, data-driven policing reforms implemented across nine Brazilian states.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Using a staggered difference-in-differences design over 2,355 municipalities and a long municipal panel, the study estimated an average reduction of 18.3 homicides per 100,000 after implementation, with stronger effects in higher-violence settings and vulnerable groups.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This is the strongest quasi-experimental signal in the frozen Brazilian set, but its outcome is public-safety performance at the municipal level.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: It should not be reinterpreted as proof of individual officer fitness, health, or tactical proficiency.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The Escola Segura evaluation provides an equally important counterweight.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The program placed retired or reserve military police in state schools, and its impact on perceived safety, victimization, graffiti, and illicit-drug use was estimated using a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences comparison between a treated school and a similar untreated school.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The study reported no impact on the analyzed outcomes.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Preserving this null result is central to the evidence-governance model: readiness-oriented policy should not assume that a plausible or visible intervention is effective merely because it has institutional support.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Together, these studies show why organizational readiness must include evaluation capacity.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Data-driven management can be associated with large public-safety effects under a credible identification strategy, while another security program can show no measurable impact on selected outcomes.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This contrast argues for outcome specification before implementation, transparent analytic plans, and the use of designs capable of separating program effects from secular trends.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Yet the mapped literature does not provide a mature body of CFIR-, ERIC-, Proctor-, or RE-AIM-style implementation research in Brazilian public safety.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The unresolved label is therefore STRUCTURAL_METHODS_GAP — FORMAL IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE IN BRAZILIAN PUBLIC SAFETY.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Physical and Academy Readiness
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Physical readiness is represented by an observational longitudinal study of 219 male military police recruits in Tocantins.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Health-related physical fitness was measured before and after six months of mandatory academy training, with an earlier assessment after a seven-month unsupervised period.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The recruits maintained high fitness before academy entry and improved across all measured fitness components during the academy; reported average changes ranged from 7.7% to 69.0%, while cardiorespiratory fitness improved by less than 10%.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The study demonstrates that measurable fitness changed over an academy period, but because there was no external control group and the academy included multiple simultaneous exposures, the data cannot isolate which training components caused the improvements.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: This distinction matters operationally.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Academy fitness gains show that readiness is modifiable during structured training, but they do not define the optimal program, the durability of gains after graduation, or the relationship between test improvement and field performance.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: A readiness system should therefore track both capacity and transfer: aerobic fitness, strength/endurance, and other physical metrics are relevant, but they should be linked prospectively to occupational tasks, injury, fatigue, attendance, recovery, and retention rather than treated as ends in themselves.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: The Supporting martial-arts study adds a different perspective.
Notes: Numbers map only to numbered bibliography; no thematic inference.

Exact_Sentence: Thirty-four cadets were grouped according to supplemental Brazilian jiu-jitsu, Muay Thai/kickboxing, or no supplemental martial-arts experience and completed a simulated domestic-violence use-of-force call.

Exact_Sentence: This synthesis shows a field with meaningful signals but uneven evidentiary depth.
